column1: # ALREADY SATISFY `cond` — keys preserved for a map, order for a list.
# "Already satisfies" is the meet CHANGING NOTHING, not mere
# unifiability. A map is open, so `{p:2}` unifies with `{debug:true}`
# by gaining the key, and a filter that kept everything that could be
# made to match would keep everything — the first row is the case that
# settles it. The design named unifiability; its own example is
# unsatisfiable under it (see the register, G8.2 departures).
# The condition is an ordinary value, so the constraint atoms compose
# with it for free — `min(2)`, `{x:min(2)}` — and a failing child is an
# THE SAME LENGTH RULE, from the other side. `filter(bag, [])` keeps
# only the elements that unify with the empty tuple, which is none of
# them -- Go kept EVERY element, the exact opposite selection, because
# its trial meet never set the flag the length gate reads (BUGS.md
# §61). The controls are the half that says the rule is about LENGTH:
# a one-element pattern keeps only the one-element member, and `top`
# keeps both -- so the empty-pattern row above is not simply "filter
# A HOLE IN THE DATA ARGUMENT IS BOUND BY AN APPLY. `&` meets and never
# fills a hole, so the data is handed to the generator explicitly:
# `apply(v, T)` binds each hole T leaves free, here the data argument,
# while the template's own holes stay the generator's.
# THE CANDIDATES filter SEES ARE THE MEMBERS GENERATION EMITS (BUGS.md
# §79): a hidden child is never selected into the result. The rule is
# A RELATIVE PATH IN A BOUND'S ARGUMENT reads where the member a
# condition tries lands, as any other term of the condition does (#506).
# A CONDITION IN A MEMBER A GENERATOR MAKES reads that member as one in a
# written member does: the filter waits until the member is in place.
# A climb counts from the filter's own key, so `...lim` under `p.x.f`
# names `p.lim`, in a made member and a written one alike.

column3: l: [1, 2, 3]\np: pack({a: 1, b: 3}, {lim: _, f: filter($.l, above(..lim))})
folders: {a: {parent: "-"}, b: {parent: a}, c: {parent: a}, d: {parent: b}}\nsubs: pack($.folders, {id: key(), kids: filter($.folders, {parent: ...id})})
